A configuration system (100) for configuring a first device (130) in a lighting system is disclosed. The configuration system (100) comprises a memory (102) arranged for storing one or more light settings (110), which light settings (110) are defined by one or more light setting rules (112). The configuration system (100) further comprises a communication unit (104) arranged for communicating with the first device (130). The configuration system (100) further comprises a processor (106) arranged for identifying a device property (132) of the first device (130) based on information received from the first device (130) via the communication unit (104). The processor (106) is further arranged for accessing one or more light settings (110) stored in the memory (102), and for associating the device property (132) with at least one of the one or more light setting rules (112) of at least one of the one or more light settings (110) only if the device property (132) is compliant with the respective light setting rule (112), and for storing the association. This method allows a user to connect the first device (130) to the configuration system (100), whereupon the configuration system (100) determines the functionality of the first device (130) in the lighting system based on the light settings (110) stored in the memory (102).

outputs.L3:
The configuration system is designed to store one or more light settings in memory. Each light setting is defined by one or more light setting rules, which specify how particular devices or device properties should be handled within the lighting system.

The system includes a communication unit configured to communicate with a first device that is part of, or intended to be connected to, the lighting system. Through this communication unit, the system receives information from the first device. This information may relate to the device’s capabilities, type, configuration, status, or other relevant characteristics.

A processor in the system uses the received information to identify at least one property of the first device. Once the property has been identified, the processor compares it with the stored light setting rules. The processor associates the identified device property with a particular light setting rule only when the property complies with, or satisfies, the requirements of that rule.

In this way, the system allows a user to connect a device to the lighting system without having to manually configure all aspects of its operation. The functionality of the connected device within the lighting system is determined automatically based on the stored light settings and the rules associated with those settings. This enables a more efficient and user-friendly configuration process, while ensuring that the device operates in accordance with predefined lighting behavior.
outputs.L4:
A configuration system for a lighting system is provided to automatically configure a connected device when the device is introduced into the system. The lighting system may include one or more luminaires, lamps, sensors, switches, controllers, gateways, or other lighting-related devices that communicate with a central controller or configuration unit. The configuration system stores a plurality of predefined light setting rules, where each rule defines one or more lighting functions, operating parameters, control relationships, or permitted configurations for devices having particular properties.

When a new device is connected to the lighting system, the configuration system establishes communication with the device and obtains information identifying the device’s properties. These properties may include, for example, the device type, manufacturer, model number, supported communication protocol, dimming capability, color capability, maximum light output, sensor type, location, address, or other operational characteristics. The system may receive this information directly from the device, retrieve it from a database, or determine it through interrogation, discovery, or commissioning procedures.

After the device properties have been identified, the configuration system compares them with the stored light setting rules. Based on this comparison, the system determines which rules are applicable to the connected device and which lighting functions the device is capable of performing. The system then selects one or more compliant light setting rules and uses them to assign a function or role to the device within the lighting system. For example, the system may determine that a connected device is a dimmable luminaire and assign it to a dimming group, identify it as a color-tunable lamp and apply appropriate color-control settings, or recognize it as an occupancy sensor and link it to one or more lights that should respond to detected motion.

By automatically matching device properties to rule-defined light settings, the configuration system reduces or eliminates the need for manual setup by a user or installer. The system can determine how a newly connected device should operate, what settings should be applied, and how the device should interact with other components of the lighting system. This simplifies installation, improves consistency of configuration, and helps ensure that each connected device is used only in a manner that is compatible with its capabilities and the overall rules of the lighting system.

As a result, when a new device is added, the lighting system can automatically recognize the device, determine its functionality, and assign appropriate settings or control relationships without requiring detailed user input. This provides a more efficient and user-friendly commissioning process and allows the lighting system to adapt more easily as devices are added, replaced, or reconfigured.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a European patent application summary describing a system with a memory, communication unit, and processor for automatically determining the functionality of a newly connected device in a lighting system.
counterfactuals.output:
**Summary**

The invention relates to a system for automatically determining a functionality of a newly connected device in a lighting system. The lighting system comprises a plurality of lighting devices and/or control devices interconnected by a wired or wireless communication network. When a new device is connected to the lighting system, it is desirable to identify the type and available functions of the device without requiring manual configuration by an installer or user.

According to an aspect of the invention, a system is provided comprising a memory, a communication unit, and a processor. The communication unit is configured to communicate with devices in the lighting system, including a newly connected device. The memory stores device identification information, functional profiles, communication protocol information, and/or rules for determining device functionality. The processor is configured to detect connection of the newly connected device, obtain device data from the newly connected device via the communication unit, and determine, based on the obtained device data and information stored in the memory, one or more functionalities supported by the newly connected device.

The obtained device data may comprise, for example, a device identifier, manufacturer identifier, product type, firmware version, supported commands, sensor capabilities, actuator capabilities, power characteristics, network address, or a response to one or more interrogation commands. The processor may compare the obtained device data with one or more stored functional profiles. If a matching profile is found, the processor assigns the corresponding functionality to the newly connected device. If no exact match is found, the processor may determine the functionality by analysing responses of the newly connected device to test commands, by querying an external database via the communication unit, or by applying inference rules stored in the memory.

The determined functionality may indicate whether the newly connected device is, for example, a luminaire, light source, driver, dimmer, switch, occupancy sensor, daylight sensor, gateway, controller, emergency lighting unit, or another lighting-system component. The determined functionality may further include supported lighting functions such as switching, dimming, colour control, colour temperature adjustment, scene control, sensor reporting, scheduling, diagnostics, or energy monitoring.

After determining the functionality, the processor may automatically configure the newly connected device for operation within the lighting system. This may include assigning the device to a group, zone, scene, control rule, network address, or security domain. The processor may also update a topology or configuration model stored in the memory and make the determined functionality available to a user interface, a lighting controller, or another system component.

The system reduces installation effort and configuration errors by enabling automatic recognition and commissioning of newly connected devices in a lighting system. The invention is particularly suitable for building lighting installations, smart lighting networks, office lighting systems, industrial lighting systems, and connected home lighting systems.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following concept into patent language: when a lighting device is connected, a controller reads its capabilities, compares them to predefined lighting scene rules in memory, links compatible rules to the device, and uses that to determine what the device can do.
counterfactuals.output:
A lighting control system comprising a controller configured to, upon detection of connection of a lighting device to the lighting control system, obtain capability information associated with the lighting device, the capability information identifying one or more controllable lighting functions supported by the lighting device. The controller is further configured to access a memory storing a plurality of predefined lighting scene rules, each lighting scene rule defining one or more lighting operations and one or more capability requirements for execution of the lighting operation. The controller compares the obtained capability information with the capability requirements of the plurality of predefined lighting scene rules, identifies one or more lighting scene rules compatible with the lighting device, and associates the identified compatible lighting scene rules with the lighting device. The controller thereafter determines, based at least in part on the associated compatible lighting scene rules, a set of lighting operations that are available for control of the lighting device.

In one embodiment, the capability information comprises at least one of dimming capability, color temperature capability, color-changing capability, beam-shaping capability, intensity range, supported control protocol, address information, power rating, sensor capability, or firmware-supported function. The predefined lighting scene rules may comprise rules defining illumination level, color, color temperature, transition timing, dynamic lighting effect, grouping behavior, or scene participation criteria. By automatically associating compatible lighting scene rules with the connected lighting device, the controller enables configuration of the lighting device without requiring manual selection of device-specific scene parameters.

A method of configuring a lighting device in a lighting control system comprises detecting connection of the lighting device, reading capability information from or for the lighting device, retrieving predefined lighting scene rules from a memory, comparing the capability information with capability requirements specified by the predefined lighting scene rules, linking to the lighting device those lighting scene rules determined to be compatible with the capability information, and determining controllable functions of the lighting device based on the linked lighting scene rules.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
